gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Outdoor Life measured the OUPES Mega 1's AC port and inverter drawing 50 W on their own, against 10 W for the EcoFlow DELTA 2 and 25 W for the Anker SOLIX C1000. That is why the Mega 1 delivered only 60% of its rated 1,024 Wh at a steady 34 W load but 92% at 380 W.
standout_why: I read four of the result pages in full. Make Tech Easier (Kris Wouk, 1100W, updated 2024-01-28), Active Gear Review (Nazar Kluchkovskiy, Exodus 1200, 2025-01-16), NerdTechy (1100W, 2021-09-04) and ShopSavvy's Exodus 1200 TLDR (2026-02-15) contain no measured figure at all: no usable Wh, efficiency, idle draw, measured charge rate or noise level. They only repeat specs such as 992 Wh, 1,200 W and a 600 W AC input. The three oupes.com result pages are the maker's own spec and sales pages, and I didn't open them because the site returned HTTP 429. None of the pages gives a measured AC idle or inverter draw, measured usable capacity, or the shortfall in the Exodus 1200's AC charging.
decides: The finding does not change the pick, but it sets a condition on it. The Mega 1 is the OUPES unit with the strongest named lab results: Outdoor Life measured 92% usable at 380 W, a 43-minute recharge and 90% after three months in storage, and The Solar Lab measured 79% at 1,779 W. It wins for loads of a few hundred watts. For an all-night small load such as a CPAP, router or phone charging, its 50 W AC overhead wastes about 40% of the battery, so the shopper should use its DC or USB ports or choose a unit with lower idle draw. The Exodus 1200 is the weaker OUPES option. The Solar Lab could not get its AC input above 400 W against the advertised 600 W, measured about 16.5 W idle drain and 77% efficiency, and saw it shut off at 6–7% charge.

findings.label: AC port and inverter power use (Outdoor Life)
findings.source_title: The Best Portable Power Stations of 2026, Tested and Reviewed (Outdoor Life, Laura Lancaster)
findings.note: Page says 'Updated May 5, 2025'. Measured with a Kill-a-Watt meter. In the same test the EcoFlow DELTA 2 drew 10 W and the Anker SOLIX C1000 25 W. The reviewer wrote that 'its AC port was simply using a ton more power: 50 watts for the combined port and inverter.'

findings.label: Usable energy at a steady 34 W load (Outdoor Life)
findings.source_title: The Best Portable Power Stations of 2026, Tested and Reviewed (Outdoor Life, Laura Lancaster)
findings.note: Load was a grow light at about 34 W. 610/1,024 = 59.6%. Same test: EcoFlow DELTA 2 67%, Anker SOLIX C1000 62%, BLUETTI AC180 54% in the table (39.9% in the review text), EcoFlow DELTA 3 52%, Jackery Explorer 1000 Plus 49%.

findings.label: Usable energy at a steady 380 W load (Outdoor Life)
findings.value: 92% of 1,024 Wh (940 Wh) on the retest; 76% on the first run
findings.source_title: The Best Portable Power Stations of 2026, Tested and Reviewed (Outdoor Life, Laura Lancaster)
findings.note: Load was a dehumidifier at about 380 W. On the first run the unit cut out with 4% still showing on its meter. 940/1,024 = 91.8%. Same test: EcoFlow DELTA 2 88%, Anker SOLIX C1000 90%.

findings.label: Usable energy after 3 months in storage, 380 W load (Outdoor Life)
findings.source_title: The Best Portable Power Stations of 2026, Tested and Reviewed (Outdoor Life, Laura Lancaster)
findings.note: Stored in a garage at about 60–75°F, then retested. Same test: EcoFlow DELTA 2 83%, Anker SOLIX C1000 86%.

findings.label: AC recharge time, measured (Outdoor Life)
findings.source_title: The Best Portable Power Stations of 2026, Tested and Reviewed (Outdoor Life, Laura Lancaster)
findings.note: Same test: EcoFlow DELTA 2 1 h 15 min, Anker SOLIX C1000 1.4 h. The reviewer also confirmed 2,000 W maximum output.

findings.label: Inverter efficiency at a high load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: OUPES Mega 1 Review: Affordable and Powerful or Too Good to Be True? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The page is undated. Full charge run down at 1,779 W. 1,024 Wh / 1,779 W = 34.5 min in theory, and 27 / 34.5 ≈ 78%, which the site rounds to 79%. The unit shut off at 2%. The reviewers called the fans 'very, very loud' but gave no dB figure.

findings.label: AC charging input achieved vs advertised (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: under 400 W achieved vs 600 W advertised; full charge took over 4 h
findings.source_title: OUPES Exodus 1200 Review: Good Deal or Complete Failure? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The page is undated. Reviewers: 'we couldn't hit an AC input over 400W' in Fast Charging mode. Active Gear Review, one of ChatGPT's results, repeats '0% to 80% in just 72 minutes' without having measured it.

findings.label: Inverter efficiency (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: OUPES Exodus 1200 Review: Good Deal or Complete Failure? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 992 Wh / 1,198 W = 49.7 min in theory, and 38.5 / 49.7 = 77%. Shut off at about 6–7% remaining. In the 1,500 W boost test it delivered about 1,300 W.

findings.label: Idle self-drain with nothing plugged in (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: OUPES Exodus 1200 Review: Good Deal or Complete Failure? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Battery fell from about 78% to 36% over 24 h. Check: 42% × 992 Wh = 417 Wh / 24 h ≈ 17.4 W, so the site's 16.5 W is a rough figure.

findings.label: Inverter efficiency and AC charge time (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 83% (44 min at 2,330 W); 2 h 7 min full charge from the wall
findings.source_title: OUPES Mega 2 Power Station Review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The page is undated. 2,048 Wh / 2,330 W = 52.7 min in theory, and 44 / 52.7 ≈ 83%. The unit shut off immediately at a 3,000 W load. Reviewers struggled to get more than 800 W solar from four 200 W panels and noted noticeable idle drain without measuring it.

findings.label: Inverter efficiency and AC charge time (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 86% (53.5 min at 2,968 W); just over 2 h from 2% to 100%
findings.source_title: OUPES Mega 3 Power Station Review: Affordable Powerhouse or Major Oops? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The page is undated. 3,072 Wh / 2,968 W = 62.1 min in theory, and 53.5 / 62.1 = 86%. Shut off at 2%.

findings.label: Efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: OUPES Exodus 2400 Review: Budget Redemption or a Total Miss? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The page is undated and doesn't give the load or runtime for the efficiency test. Surge was unreliable much above 2,500 W.

findings.label: Measured AC wall charge time and solar charge (Bob Vila)
findings.value: under 1.5 h from AC; about 2.5 days from 15% to 97% on a 100 W panel
findings.source_title: OUPES Mega 1 Review (Bob Vila, Mark Wolfe)
findings.note: Published 2025-09-24 after a 3-week test. The reviewer said the weather was uncooperative during the solar run.

unsourced: Noise in dB for any OUPES unit: The Solar Lab, Bob Vila and Outdoor Life describe fan noise only in words, and I found no named measurement.
TechRadar's 86% efficiency figure for the Mega 2: the review page at techradar.com/pro/oupes-mega-2-review returned no body text, so I could not check the figure or how it was measured.
Usable Wh for the Exodus 1200, Mega 2 or Mega 3 from a low-load Kill-a-Watt style test like Outdoor Life's: none found. The Solar Lab tested only near full inverter load.
Publish dates for The Solar Lab reviews: the pages show only a 2026 copyright footer, and a bash curl attempt to read their page metadata was blocked.
Which OUPES models and prices are current on oupes.com: the collection page returned HTTP 429, so I didn't confirm today's lineup or prices.
